mainTopic: How the רבנן and רבי אליעזר read ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״, whether רבי אליעזר's disqualification brings כרת, and the ברייתא about leaving blood overnight
overview: The גמרא continues a debate from the משנה. רבי אליעזר says a קרבן becomes invalid if the כהן plans to eat something normally burned, or burn something normally eaten, and the רבנן disagree. First the גמרא shows how the רבנן use the double word ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״ for other lessons. Then it shows רבי אליעזר's answer: the change in the word's form teaches two things. רבי זירא then asks why, if the source is the פיגול verse, there is no כרת, especially since רבי יוחנן said רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת. רב אסי answers that תנאים disagree about whether רבי אליעזר's disqualification is from the תורה or only rabbinic. To show this, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about mixed-up thoughts and about planning to leave the blood overnight, where רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר both speak. The גמרא first suggests that the two differ about כרת. It then rejects this and says the ברייתא holds three separate disputes, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The רבנן's use of the double word: eating language and burning language are the same
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the doubled ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״ to teach that a wrong thought counts whether it is worded as 'eating' for the מזבח or 'burning' on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes no difference whether he thinks using the words 'eating for the altar' or using the words 'burning on the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining what the רבנן learn from the double word in the verse, since they do not learn רבי אליעזר's rule from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in the תורה must teach something, so the רבנן need their own use for the doubling. They say it teaches that when a כהן plans to put the קומץ on the מזבח tomorrow, it is פיגול whether he calls it 'eating' or 'burning'. The two phrasings are treated as one.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes no difference; both cases are the same
Thinks or intends something during the עבודה (the source of פיגול)
Burning a part of the קרבן on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence starts in the middle. The words before it on the previous page explain that the רבנן read the doubled verse this way. This line is the end of that explanation, not a new teaching.

phrases.english: that there is no difference if he intends
phrases.notes: This continues the רבנן's reading of ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״ (ויקרא 7:18) from just before.

phrases.english: using the language of eating for the altar,
and there is no difference if he intends
using the language of burning on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא שְׁנָא כִּי מְחַשֵּׁב בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה לְמִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבנן's explanation of the doubled verse, begun before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative use of an extra word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubling seems to force רבי אליעזר's rule, which the רבנן reject.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן use the doubling to equate 'eating' wording with 'burning' wording for פיגול.

steps.title: Another option for the רבנן: the כזית measure applies to burning too
steps.stepSummary: Or the doubling teaches that a כזית is needed for burning just as for eating. The word 'eating' still means eating in the normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: just as eating is with a כזית, so too burning is with a כזית. And really, 'eating' means eating in the usual way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן a second possible use for the double word: the minimum amount of a כזית applies to a thought about burning, just as it applies to a thought about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong thought only makes the קרבן פיגול if it is about at least a כזית. The doubling links burning to eating, so the כזית rule covers burning too. The last line closes the door on רבי אליעזר's reading. 'Eating' keeps its normal meaning, so eating something meant for the מזבח does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's bulk, the minimum amount that counts
But really; restates the main point
In the usual way; the normal manner

phrases.english: Alternatively, just as eating is with an olive-bulk –
so too burning is with an olive-bulk,
and really, eating means in the usual way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, מָה אֲכִילָה בִּכְזַיִת – אַף הַקְטָרָה בִּכְזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different use of the doubled verse for the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second alternative use of the extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubling might teach that eating what is normally burned counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches the כזית measure for burning, and eating keeps its normal meaning.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's answer: the change in the word's form teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that a simple doubling would have used the same form twice. The change from הֵאָכֹל to יֵאָכֵל shows the verse teaches both lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He says: if so, the Torah should have written 'אִם הֵאָכֹל הֵאָכֹל' or 'אִם יֵאָכֵל יֵאָכֵל.' Why does it say 'הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי אליעזר responds to the רבנן. The verse doesn't just repeat a word; it changes its form, so it has room for two teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse only wanted to teach what the רבנן say, a plain repetition with the same form would have been enough. Since the Torah used two different forms, רבי אליעזר learns both: the רבנן's lesson, and his own rule. His rule is that eating what is normally burned, or burning what is normally eaten, makes the קרבן invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah (literally, 'the Merciful One') write
'Is surely eaten': the doubled word in the verse, in two different forms

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן use the doubled word for one lesson only. רבי אליעזר says the change in form allows two lessons, which includes his own rule about eating and burning switched around.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer? If so,
let the Merciful One write: "If he'akhol he'akhol,"
or else: "If ye'akhel ye'akhel."
Why does it say "he'akhol ye'akhel"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's readings by showing the verse has room for both lessons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the רבנן found a use for the doubling, רבי אליעזר's source seems to be gone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change in form teaches both the רבנן's lesson and רבי אליעזר's rule.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: then why not כרת too?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רב אסי. If רבי אליעזר's source is this verse, it should also bring a punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי: If רבי אליעזר's reason is because of this, then one should also be liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the reasoning just given for רבי אליעזר. If the verse treats both kinds of eating as the same, the full punishment of פיגול, כרת, should apply too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר learns his rule from the פיגול verse itself, his case should count as full פיגול. Full פיגול carries כרת for whoever eats it, not just an invalid קרבן. So the source seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual 'cutting off', the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Asi:
But if the reason of Rabbi Eliezer
is because of this,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the reading of ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״ from the step before.

phrases.english: let one also be liable to karet?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי: וְאִי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source just given for רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אליעזר learns his rule from ״הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same verse brings כרת for פיגול, so a rule learned from it should also carry כרת.

steps.title: Blocking the escape: רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת
steps.stepSummary: One cannot answer that רבי אליעזר does hold of כרת. רב אסי himself said, in the name of רבי יוחנן, that רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that indeed there is כרת, but you yourself said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי אליעזר admits that there is no punishment of כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא shuts down a possible answer to his question. He reminds רב אסי of his own report that רבי אליעזר does not hold there is כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy way out would be to say that רבי אליעזר really does hold there is כרת. But רב אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, said that רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת. So the question stands: how can the source be the פיגול verse while the punishment is missing?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say that indeed it is so

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes רבי זירא's question sharp: רבי יוחנן seems to give רבי אליעזר a source from the פיגול verse, yet also says there is no כרת. The next step settles this by showing that תנאים disagree about רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: And if you would say that indeed it is so,
but aren't you the one who said
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר שֶׁאֵין עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת!
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer concedes that it is not punishable by karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question by ruling out the answer that רבי אליעזר holds there is כרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible answer that רבי אליעזר does hold there is כרת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אסי's own report from רבי יוחנן says רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת, so that answer fails.

steps.title: רב אסי: תנאים argue about רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that תנאים disagree about רבי אליעזר. Some say his disqualification is from the Torah, and some say it is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is a disagreement between תנאים about רבי אליעזר's view. One says the offering is disqualified by Torah law. Another says it is only disqualified by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers רבי זירא's question about why there is no כרת. He says there are two different versions of what רבי אליעזר holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר's פסול is from the Torah, it comes from the פסוק and should bring כרת. That is the view behind רבי יוחנן's derivation from the verse. If it is only rabbinic, there is no כרת. That is the view behind רבי יוחנן saying רבי אליעזר admits there is no כרת. So רבי יוחנן's two statements reflect two different תנאים, and they do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים (sages of the משנה era)

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer removes the contradiction between רבי יוחנן's two statements about רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a dispute of tannaim
phrases.notes: This is רב אסי answering רבי זירא's question from the previous step.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Eliezer.
There is one who says: it is unfit by Torah law,
and there is one who says: it is unfit by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 4-5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the view into two versions held by different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's verse-based source and his 'no כרת' statement contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each statement follows a different תנא's version of רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא about mixed-up thoughts and leaving blood overnight
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: slaughtering with a plan to drink the blood, burn the meat, or eat the altar parts tomorrow is כשר, but רבי אליעזר disqualifies. On planning to leave the blood until tomorrow, רבי יהודה disqualifies, and רבי אלעזר says this is the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If someone slaughters an offering planning to drink some of its blood tomorrow, or burn some of its meat tomorrow, or eat some of its altar parts tomorrow, the offering is כשר. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it. If he plans to leave some of its blood until tomorrow, רבי יהודה disqualifies it. רבי אלעזר said: Even in this case רבי אליעזר disqualifies and the חכמים declare it כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the dispute about רבי אליעזר. It sets up the questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each plan in the first part is 'mixed up.' Blood belongs on the מזבח, not in a person's mouth. Meat is for people to eat, not for burning. אימורים are for the מזבח, not for eating. The חכמים say a thought like this does not make the offering פיגול. Then the ברייתא adds a milder case: just planning to leave the blood overnight, without using it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
To leave over, to set aside

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר (אליעזר) and רבי אלעזר (אלעזר) are two different people with very similar names. Read carefully!

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who slaughters the offering
to drink from its blood tomorrow,
to burn from its meat tomorrow,
to eat from its altar portions tomorrow – it is fit,
and Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies.
To leave over from its blood until tomorrow –
Rabbi Yehuda disqualifies.
Rabbi Elazar said: Even in this case
Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies and the Sages declare it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לִשְׁתּוֹת מִדָּמוֹ לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that shows the dispute between תנאים claimed in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים disagree about the nature of רבי אליעזר's disqualification.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר on leaving blood until tomorrow.

steps.title: Whose view does רבי יהודה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion רבי יהודה's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה – according to whose view is he speaking?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts analyzing the ברייתא by asking which side רבי יהודה is on. This sets up the next two moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible sides: the רבנן, who say a mixed-up thought is כשר, or רבי אליעזר, who disqualifies. The גמרא will test each option.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda – according to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an analysis of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה follows the רבנן or רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: It cannot follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן call a mixed-up 'eating' thought כשר, then surely just planning to leave the blood is כשר. So רבי יהודה cannot be following them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he follows the רבנן: Look, there, where he thinks in terms of eating, the רבנן still say it is כשר. Here, then, all the more so it should be כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first option, that רבי יהודה follows the רבנן. It uses a כל שכן argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the person had a stronger thought: actually eating or drinking it tomorrow. Even so, the רבנן say it is כשר. Just leaving the blood, with no use at all, is a weaker thought. So the רבנן would certainly call it כשר, and they could not agree with רבי יהודה's פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now' – introduces an argument from a stronger case

phrases.english: If you say according to the Rabbis –
now, if there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the first case of the ברייתא: drinking the blood, burning the meat, or eating the אימורים.

phrases.english: where he has an intention in terms of eating,
the Rabbis declare it fit,
here, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן – הַשְׁתָּא, וּמָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that רבי יהודה follows the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: By a כל שכן, the רבנן would surely call the weaker 'leaving' case כשר.

steps.title: If it follows רבי אליעזר, רבי אלעזר adds nothing
steps.stepSummary: So רבי יהודה must follow רבי אליעזר. But then רבי אלעזר says the same thing, that רבי אליעזר disqualifies here, so the two seem identical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he follows רבי אליעזר. But then רבי אלעזר said: Even in this case רבי אליעזר disqualifies and the חכמים declare it כשר. So רבי אלעזר is the same as רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, that רבי יהודה follows רבי אליעזר. It then points out a problem: רבי אלעזר would be saying nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר say that, according to רבי אליעזר, leaving the blood is פסול, then they agree completely. So why does the ברייתא quote them as two separate statements? This leaves the גמרא needing to find a real difference between them.
steps.whatToRemember: Neither option works smoothly yet. רבי יהודה cannot follow the רבנן because of the כל שכן. If he follows רבי אליעזר, he seems identical to רבי אלעזר. The גמרא must find a difference between them.

phrases.english: Rather, it is according to Rabbi Eliezer,
and yet Rabbi Elazar said: Even in this case
Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies and the Sages declare it fit.
Rabbi Elazar is the same as Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 rules out the רבנן, this step tries רבי אליעזר and finds a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's quoting רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר as two separate opinions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both describe רבי אליעזר disqualifying the 'leaving' case, their statements are identical and one of them is unnecessary.

steps.title: Suggestion: The difference between them is about כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר differ about כרת. According to רבי יהודה, in רבי אליעזר's view leaving the blood is only פסול, but the other cases also bring כרת. According to רבי אלעזר, both are פסול with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the difference between them about כרת? רבי יהודה holds that planning to leave the blood is just a disqualification, but in those other cases one is also liable to כרת. And רבי אלעזר comes to say that in both cases the offering is disqualified and there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to solve the problem from the last step by finding a real difference between רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר. It says they argue about whether there is כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, both רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר seemed to say only 'רבי אליעזר disqualifies.' Now the גמרא says רבי יהודה sees the other cases (drinking blood, burning meat, eating altar parts tomorrow) as stronger, strong enough for כרת. רבי אלעזר says nothing here is that strong. If this were right, it would show תנאים disagree about how serious רבי אליעזר's disqualification is, which fits רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
This one and that one; both cases

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא will not accept that two sages said the exact same thing. It looks for a real difference.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that כרת is the difference between them?
That רבי יהודה holds:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets ('the first תנא'), but the corrected wording leaves them out.

phrases.english: To leave the blood is merely a disqualification,
but in those cases one is also liable to כרת,
phrases.notes: 'Those cases' are the ones from the ברייתא in step 7: drinking the blood, burning the meat, or eating the altar parts tomorrow.

phrases.english: and רבי אלעזר comes to say:

phrases.aramaic: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָּרֵת!
phrases.english: in both this case and that case it is disqualified and there is no כרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 10 (רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר look identical) by proposing a real difference about כרת.
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's claim that תנאים disagree about how serious רבי אליעזר's disqualification is
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in step 7, read so that רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר differ about כרת

steps.title: Rejection: No כרת for anyone, and there are three disputes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the כרת idea. Everyone agrees there is no כרת. Instead the ברייתא holds three different disputes. The first is the תנא קמא: רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue only in the other cases, and leaving the blood is כשר according to all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees there is no כרת. Here there are three disputes about the matter. The תנא קמא holds that they argue only in those cases, but about leaving the blood, everyone agrees it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that the argument is about כרת. It starts a new explanation: the ברייתא contains three disputes. This step gives the first one and sets up the next two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of one disagreement about punishment, the גמרא says the three voices disagree about which cases רבי אליעזר even disqualifies. The תנא קמא limits the argument to the other cases. Leaving the blood is כשר according to everyone. The views of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר come next, beyond this step.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
The words of all; everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: 'Everyone agrees there is no כרת' is talking about רבי אליעזר's view. Even he does not give כרת for these mixed-up thoughts. It does not mean the offering is fine.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees there is no כרת,
and here there are three disputes about the matter:
the תנא קמא holds that they disagree in those cases,
but about leaving the blood, everyone agrees it is valid,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 11's כרת explanation and replaces it with a three-way dispute structure.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר differ about כרת, so the proof for רב אסי falls away.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read with no one holding כרת. The difference between the opinions is about which cases are disqualified at all.
